Merge bitcoin-core/gui#955: qt: filter addhdkey from RPC console history

31467d59a5a8e6721af1dc5d6592fad31339bcb9 qt: filter addhdkey from RPC console history (Mateusz Klatt)

Pull request description:

  Filters `addhdkey` arguments from RPC console history, consistent with other RPCs that handle private key material.

  This prevents extended private keys from being retained in history. It also covers the mnemonic and passphrase inputs proposed in bitcoin/bitcoin#35857.

  Adds a parser test verifying that the arguments are redacted.

  ## Motivation

  `addhdkey` accepts a BIP 32 extended private key, but its arguments are currently retained in RPC console history, unlike other RPCs that handle private key material.

  The same filter would also protect the mnemonic and passphrase inputs proposed in bitcoin/bitcoin#35857.

  ## Changes

  - Add `addhdkey` to the RPC console sensitive-command filter.
  - Add a parser test verifying that its arguments are redacted as `addhdkey(…)`.

  ## Tests

  - `./build_gui/bin/test_bitcoin-qt` — all tests passed, including `RPCNestedTests::rpcNestedTests()`.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36669: refactor: store positions as a 64 bits integer in flatfiles

48092a9042d8fcfd6bb7ae5911a1d53b8746d546 flatfile: use 64-bit file positioning syscalls in Windows (Antoine Poinsot)
17556cb1f52fcbc807f65245101f72e8ec1573d8 flatfile: store position as a 64 bits integer (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  That field is the last 32-bit in flat files management that is only bounded indirectly by callers' usage (unlike the file number for instance). In the spirit of the ongoing effort to avoid unnecessarily using 32 bits integers or platform specific types (for instance #24214, #33724, #34109, #35097, #35616), i was scanning for fields it could be prudent to promote to prevent any possible future misuse. This one is a good candidate because it does not change on-disk representation, since we serialize positions as varints.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36667: net: enforce timeout interval for paused send peers

cc2534cdf7b14d0f1a18928ebaab7f7fdd7e839e net: enforce timeout interval for paused send peers (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  Today it's possible to keep some peers running ancient versions paused for a long time. If such a peer is so slow to read as to not drain our send buffer down to the 1MB threshold within a reasonable time frame, we really shouldn't be wasting a connection slot on them. I picked 20 minutes as the reasonable time frame, since it's what we already use for ping timeouts today.

commit.message:
net: enforce timeout interval for paused send peers

No need to waste a connection slot on a peer that is so slow to read as to not
drain our send buffer down to the 1MB threshold within 20 minutes.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36665: sock: align exception monitoring between poll() and select() backends

1e0c407377034e9cbb4d52f1f534c06cdf202a36 sock: align exception monitoring between poll() and select() backends (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  On non-Linux platforms, `WaitMany` monitors every socket for exceptional conditions, even when we are not looking to read from it. On Linux, it never monitors those.

  Monitoring for certain socket events on some platforms but not others is inconsistent and surprising. In this instance it probably means these cases receive less testing as well, since they are ignored on our most well-tested platform.

  Fix this issue by only monitoring for exceptional conditions (which is necessary to detect failed connection attempts early on Windows) for sockets we are also waiting to read from.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36616: test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted

b469ff8fddb6594b69d564cca436b7baa8ed99bb test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  When a node restarts with extra_args it loses its original extra_args, so the `-whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` set by `noban_tx_relay` is lost and the node falls back to the normal tx relay delays.

  This changes `noban_tx_relay` to set `whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` in `extra_confs` instead, so it is kept across restarts.

  This speeds up some tests (running locally `build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j=18 --randomseed=1`):

  mempool_ephemeral_dust.py 49s -> 18s
  mempool_accept_wtxid.py 17s ->  6s
  wallet_fundrawtransaction.py 11s -> 7s

  Accumulated 1152s -> 1110s
  Wall 80s -> 75s

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36616: test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted

b469ff8fddb6594b69d564cca436b7baa8ed99bb test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  When a node restarts with extra_args it loses its original extra_args, so the `-whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` set by `noban_tx_relay` is lost and the node falls back to the normal tx relay delays.

  This changes `noban_tx_relay` to set `whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` in `extra_confs` instead, so it is kept across restarts.

  This speeds up some tests (running locally `build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j=18 --randomseed=1`):

  mempool_ephemeral_dust.py 49s -> 18s
  mempool_accept_wtxid.py 17s ->  6s
  wallet_fundrawtransaction.py 11s -> 7s

  Accumulated 1152s -> 1110s
  Wall 80s -> 75s

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36581: subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows

cf30d0a4123bb4237495f04e723ce9f706c2edf2 subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  `Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

  `CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

  This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

  _edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._
